clue.text: To extract the essence takes months

parts.note: December and October, abbreviated DEC and OCT, are two months
December and October, abbreviated DEC and OCT, are two months

explanation.surface: Drawing out the essence of something is a slow process taking months.
explanation.definitionFit: To boil something down to draw out its flavour or active substance is a synonym for extracting its essence.

clue.text: One seen inside local ice-skating venue during local match, not alongside

indicators.note: the rink is placed within what is left of the match
not removes the letters for alongside from the match

parts.note: a derby is a match between local rivals
by means beside, alongside
a rink is an ice-skating venue

explanation.surface: Someone watches from a skating rink during a local derby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is British slang for the neighbourhood pub, so the definition is a pub regular; a derby is a game between teams from the same area.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's regular customer, who takes alcohol there, is found in the local.

clue.text: Concentrated campaign causing Conservative damage, nauseating

parts.note: harm means damage
offensive means nauseating, repellent

explanation.surface: A political push that ends up harming the Tories in a sickening way.
explanation.definitionFit: A concentrated campaign of flattery and friendliness to win people over is this phrase.

clue.text: Confinement which sounds yellow?

indicators.note: which sounds marks a homophone of the descriptive word

parts.note: custardy means like custard, yellow in colour

explanation.surface: A jokey question whether being locked up is a yellowish thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held in jail or detention is confinement.

clue.text: Aggressively speak to lettuce during pretence

indicators.note: the lettuce sits within the pretence, as an event falls during a period

parts.note: an act is a pretence, as in 'putting on an act'
cos is a variety of lettuce

explanation.surface: Someone harangues another person about salad while putting on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach and address someone boldly or aggressively is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Religious leader has a cheek entering church

indicators.note: the other letters go into the church abbreviation

parts.note: lip means cheek, insolence

explanation.surface: A cleric is cheeky on arriving at church.
explanation.definitionFit: The title for a Muslim ruler held as successor to Muhammad, a religious leader.

clue.text: See 2
Extremity, one formed inside another

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed within the other extremity

parts.note: another extremity, here a tail

indicators.note: formed means shaped anew, rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: One part of the body grows inside another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is short for another extremity, the body's rear end appendage; the definition and the container both play on extremities.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard plate on the end of a toe is at an extremity of the body.

clue.text: Propose cryptic by Tommy, thus setter's mess cleared up

indicators.note: cryptic suggests the letters are disguised by rearranging them

parts.note: Tommy Cooper was a British comedian and magician

explanation.surface: The setter proposes a cryptic clue about a comedian and his own mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'setter' is not Paul but a dog, and its mess is cleaned up with this device.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoop for collecting dog droppings clears up a dog's mess, the setter being a breed of dog.

clue.text: Capital city a distance of 3,960 feet back

indicators.note: the whole assembled run is read in the opposite direction
3,960 feet is three quarters of the 5,280 feet in a mile, so only three of the four letters of the word are kept

parts.note: a mile is a distance

explanation.surface: A capital city sits a precise number of feet behind the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of 3,960 feet' keeps three quarters of MILE, giving MIL; A plus MIL is AMIL, and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru.

clue.text: Criminal, one moving quickly to catch police out having hidden diamonds

indicators.note: the quick mover closes round the other letters as if catching them

parts.note: a shifter is one who shifts, moves fast

indicators.note: out signals the remaining letters are rearranged
the diamonds are put away, so their letters are removed from the word police

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A fast-moving thief evades the police, having stashed stolen diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having hidden' strips the diamonds' slang word from the force's name before 'out' scrambles what is left; 'to catch' makes the quick mover surround it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who takes goods from shops is one kind of criminal.

clue.text: A novel smell, thus armpits exposed?

parts.note: Kim is a novel by Rudyard Kipling
BO is body odour, a smell

explanation.surface: Reading a novel, someone notices a smell coming from raised arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing hands on hips, elbows out, opens the underarms, which the cryptic definition describes playfully.

clue.text: Peacock to briefly visit bird

parts.note: to pop in is to make a brief visit
the jay is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A peacock drops by to see another bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A vain, showy, conceited person is figuratively a peacock, and an old word for a parrot.

clue.text: Here are stretchers for dicky Dick and Barry

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, so the letters of the names are disordered

explanation.surface: Two men named Dick and Barry are in a poor state and need stretchers.
explanation.walkthrough: Stretchers are not for the injured but bricks laid lengthwise in a wall; 'dicky' is British slang for weak or faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretchers are bricks laid with their long side showing, made at a works where bricks are produced.

clue.text: Deceiver to make black KwaZulu province upset

parts.note: to char is to scorch black

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the province name upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Natal is the province joined with KwaZulu in South Africa

explanation.surface: A con man stirs trouble in a South African province.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud who pretends to skills he lacks is a deceiver.

clue.text: Bottle of medicine disgusting, we hear

indicators.note: we hear marks a word that is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: vile means disgusting

explanation.surface: A complaint that the medicine in the bottle tastes foul.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glass container for liquid medicine is this word.

clue.text: Have in mind to be miserly

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb meaning intend and as an adjective meaning stingy.

clue.text: Women, those unmentioned in "One Arabian Night"?

parts.note: the Arabian Nights number a thousand and one, so naming one leaves a thousand, M in Roman numerals
others are those not mentioned

explanation.surface: Asks which women are left out of a single night's tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thousand and One Nights: name one and the unmentioned others are a thousand (M) others.
explanation.definitionFit: Mothers are women who have had children, so the plural is an example of women.

clue.text: Assent gained by EC thrice and bungled

indicators.note: bungled means messed up, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters EC written three times

explanation.surface: Agreement was reached by the European Community three times over, but badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreement or consent to a request is a formal synonym for assent.

clue.text: Ancient city of wild sheep and crossword setters

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: setters writing as 'we' refer to themselves as us

explanation.surface: An ancient city of untamed sheep and puzzle compilers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was an ancient Greek city in Asia Minor, now in Turkey.

clue.text: Totter at the bar?

parts.note: not someone staggering drunk at a bar but one who tots up, adding figures, and also the bar's serving surface

explanation.definitionFit: One who tots up figures adds or tallies them, and the bar's serving top has the same name.

clue.text: More creation sorted out for French singer shortly

indicators.note: sorted means put in order, so the letters are rearranged
shortly cuts the last letter off the singer's name

parts.note: Edith Piaf was a French singer

explanation.surface: More creative output is arranged for a French chanteuse soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is Sir Thomas More, author of the 1516 book naming an ideal society.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's book describing an ideal island state is his most famous creation.

clue.text: Blade on fire returned during fight

indicators.note: the reversed word sits inside the fight, as a moment falls during it

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or quarrel

indicators.note: returned means read backwards

parts.note: lit means on fire

explanation.surface: In a scuffle someone brings back a flaming weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: A set-to is British informal for a brief fight; 'returned' turns the burning word round before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A short thin dagger is a type of blade.

clue.text: A lack of Christmas spirit behind embrace, according to Spooner

indicators.note: the first sounds of the two words are swapped, in the manner of Reverend Spooner

parts.note: bum is British slang for the behind
a hug is an embrace

explanation.surface: A grumpy refusal to join in festive cheer, with a rude cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrooge's dismissive word for Christmas in Dickens has come to stand for a grudging lack of festive cheer.

clue.text: Important, as PM once was

definitions.meaning: John ... was UK Prime Minister from 1990 to 1997

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means significant, and is the surname of the 1990s British prime minister.

clue.text: As WMD report was, reportedly, allows for a huge responsibility on delivery?

indicators.note: reportedly marks the preceding phrase as spoken, so its sound counts

parts.note: the 2002 UK dossier on Iraq's weapons was famously said to have been sexed up
lets means allows

explanation.surface: A dig at the British government's dossier on weapons of mass destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'dodgy dossier' row accused the UK government of having 'sexed up' its report on Iraq's weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Six babies born at once are a huge responsibility once delivered, a playful definition.

clue.text: Project late ultimately, this for the sack?

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word late

explanation.surface: Someone whose project runs late fears being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse fibre from this plant is woven into hessian, the material used for sacks.

clue.text: Time for leadership of Saddam Hussein to admit end of reign

indicators.note: the leading letter of the name Saddam
the son's name lets the other letter in

parts.note: Uday Hussein was Saddam's elder son

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of reign

explanation.surface: The moment has come for Saddam Hussein's rule to concede its end.
explanation.walkthrough: Hussein is not Saddam again but his son Uday; 'to admit' puts N, the end of 'reign', inside UDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of the week is a unit of time.

clue.text: Shark offering menu without humans more reliable

indicators.note: without means the word menu loses the letters for humans

parts.note: men are humans
surer means more reliable

explanation.surface: A predator offers a menu with no people on it, which is safer.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan shark is slang for a moneylender charging extortionate interest.
